implementation_statement: No access rules existed before 2026. POL-02 (P06), which also carries the program governance rules, was approved 2026-09-14 and takes effect 2026-09-15. The one-page onboarding and offboarding checklist for employees and contractor agents is due 2026-09-30.

implementation_statement: The Office Manager creates and removes accounts in SYS-01, SYS-02, SYS-03, and SYS-05 and asks the MSP to set up devices. Gaps: no written account types or approvals; departing contractor agents keep access for up to two weeks (an agent who left on 2026-07-17 was still active on 2026-07-30); one shared global administrator account; no periodic account review.
evidence: SYS-02 and SYS-01 user exports; agent roster; P03 fieldwork note 2026-07-30

provider_if_inherited: Transaction platform vendor; property management platform vendor
implementation_statement: The SaaS platforms enforce the roles the Office Manager assigns. Gap: the transaction platform is set to office-wide visibility, so every agent can open every sale file, including other agents' clients' IDs and bank statements. Planned: limit agents to their own files by 2026-10-31.

Online banking enforces dual control on every outgoing wire and ACH batch from the escrow accounts: the Office Manager or Bookkeeper initiates and only the Broker-owner approves. The Bookkeeper, who prepares the reconciliations, cannot approve payments. Gap: the separation is a bank setting, not a written rule.
regulatory_driver: Fla. Admin. Code r. 61J2-14.010(1); Fla. Stat. 475.25(1)(k)

implementation_statement: Staff have no local administrator rights on company devices (MSP policy). Gaps: the shared global administrator account is used for routine tasks; both Transaction Coordinators hold transaction platform administrator roles they do not need.
evidence: MSP device policy; SYS-01 role list

provider_if_inherited: Productivity suite vendor; transaction platform vendor
implementation_statement: Both SaaS services lock or throttle sign-ins after repeated failures using vendor defaults (confirmed in settings).

Staff reach SaaS systems over the internet; there is no VPN. The MSP reaches company devices through its remote management tool. Gap: the company has no evidence of MFA on the MSP tool or of which technicians have access.
evidence: MSP remote tool description; MSP questionnaire (pending)

implementation_statement: Staff Wi-Fi uses WPA2 with a password changed yearly by the MSP; guest Wi-Fi is a separate network with internet access only. Contractor agents and visitors use guest Wi-Fi.

Gap: the 22 contractor agents use personal laptops and phones with company email and the transaction platform, and there are no device rules. Planned: minimum device rules in POL-02 C.3 (screen lock, updates, no shared logins, report loss in 1 hour) acknowledged by every agent, and app-level protection for the email app by 2026-12-31.

Employees watch a one-time security video at hire. Gaps: no annual training, no wire fraud training, no phishing exercises, and no training for contractor agents. Planned: annual 30-minute training for employees and agents with a wire fraud module, and quarterly phishing simulations from 2026-11.

provider_if_inherited: Productivity suite vendor; transaction platform vendor
implementation_statement: SYS-02 records sign-ins and mailbox events with the plan's default settings; SYS-01 records document views and downloads. Gap: the company has not decided which events it needs, and mailbox auditing for agents was never checked.
evidence: SYS-02 audit settings; SYS-01 activity report sample

control_name: Audit Record Review, Analysis, and Reporting
implementation_statement: Gap: nobody reviews sign-in history, forwarding rules, or download activity. Planned: a weekly 15-minute review of SYS-02 risky sign-in and new-rule reports and a monthly SYS-01 download report, recorded on a checklist, starting 2026-10.

Logs are kept for the plan's default period, which is shorter than one year. Gap: a BEC found months later could not be traced. Planned: export or extend sign-in and mailbox audit logs to 1 year by 2026-12-31.
The first independent control assessment was done 2026-08-17 to 2026-08-19 (P07). Gap: no annual cycle has been set. POL-02 A.6 now requires one each August.

The MSP keeps a device list for the 9 company devices. Gap: no list of SaaS services, of where client personal information is stored, or of contractor devices that reach company data. Planned: one-page system and data inventory by 2026-10-31.
The BIA (P05) was approved 2026-09-14. Gap: there is no contingency plan, no backup approver for escrow payments, and no hurricane checklist. Planned: a short plan from the BIA by 2026-12-31.
Gap: SYS-09 has never been restore-tested. Planned: the MSP restores a sample mailbox and folder by 2026-09-30, then quarterly, with a written result.

SYS-09 copies the 7 employee mailboxes and shared files nightly and keeps 30 days of versions; the SaaS vendors back up their own platforms. Gaps: the 22 agent mailboxes and SYS-01 files have no independent copy; one MSP administrator login can delete the backups.
evidence: Backup job report (July 2026); SYS-09 retention setting
regulatory_driver: Fla. Stat. 475.5015; Fla. Admin. Code r. 61J2-14.012(1)

implementation_statement: Every employee and agent has a named account in SYS-01, SYS-02, and SYS-03. Gap: the shared global administrator account in SYS-02 is used by two people.
Employee administrator accounts in SYS-01 and SYS-05 require MFA. Gap: the shared SYS-02 global administrator account and the SYS-09 backup console accept a password alone.

provider_if_inherited: Productivity suite vendor; transaction platform vendor
implementation_statement: All 7 employees use an authenticator app for SYS-01 and SYS-02. Gaps: the 22 contractor agents sign in with a password only, legacy sign-in protocols that bypass MFA are enabled, and SYS-03 has no MFA. Planned: MFA for every account and legacy protocols blocked by 2026-10-31.
evidence: SYS-02 MFA registration report; SYS-01 MFA setting

implementation_statement: SaaS password rules use vendor defaults. Gaps: the shared administrator password has not changed since 2023 and is known to two people; no rule against reusing personal passwords.

Gap: the identity of people who give or change payment instructions (title companies, owners, buyers) is not verified. Planned: the payment instruction verification rule in POL-03 4.9: every new or changed instruction is confirmed by a call to a number from the contract file or the party's published number, never one from the email, before money moves.

Gap: no incident handling process. The May 2026 spoofed title company email was handled by phone and not recorded. Planned: the BEC runbook (P08, approved 2026-09-14) is the handling process; first tabletop with the MSP by 2026-11-30.

Staff call the Office Manager about suspicious emails, informally. Gaps: no written reporting rule or time limit, and contractor agents do not know whom to tell. POL-03 4.2 now requires reports within 1 hour.
The BEC runbook and notification matrix (P08) were approved 2026-09-14. Gap: not yet tested; contact card and bank fraud desk numbers printed 2026-09.
Paper goes in a locked shred bin emptied by a shredding vendor. Gaps: no record of how retired devices were wiped (two laptops replaced in 2025), and no rule for deleting electronic records.
Keyed suite entry with an after-hours alarm; keys held by three employees. Gap: the storage closet with 2016 to 2020 paper files has no lock, and the cleaning crew enters after hours.
regulatory_driver: N53-R01 benchmark (314.4(c)(1)(i), physical access controls); Fla. Stat. 501.171(8)

implementation_statement: This SSP was approved by the Broker-owner on 2026-09-14 and will be reviewed each August.
Rules of behavior for employees and agents are in POL-02 Part C (approved 2026-09-14). Gap: acknowledgments not yet collected; the agent agreement has no security rules.

implementation_statement: The Broker-owner designated the Office Manager as security and compliance lead in writing on 2026-07-24 (the benchmark Qualified Individual).
Employee terminations are rare and handled the same day. Gap: contractor agents who move to another brokerage are removed only when someone notices (up to two weeks).
evidence: Agent roster vs SYS-02 and SYS-01 user lists

implementation_statement: The independent contractor agreement has a confidentiality clause. Gaps: no security duties (MFA, device rules, reporting) and no duty to return or delete client files on departure.
The first written risk assessment (P01) was completed 2026-08-07 with the MSP lead technician using NIST SP 800-30 Rev. 1, and approved 2026-09-14. POL-02 A.2 requires an update every July.

Gap: no vulnerability scanning. The MSP's tool reports missing patches only. Planned: an external scan of the office firewall and a configuration review of SYS-02 by the MSP each year, starting 2026-11.
regulatory_driver: N53-R01 benchmark (314.4(d)(2), which 314.6 would except at this size; adopted in reduced form)

implementation_statement: The transaction platform vendor's SOC 2 report was reviewed 2026-08-19 (P09). Gaps: no vendor list; no security or breach notice terms in the MSP contract; the screening provider and the property management platform vendor have never been reviewed.
The MSP-managed firewall blocks unsolicited inbound traffic, separates guest Wi-Fi, and receives quarterly firmware updates.

All SaaS services use TLS. Gap: email to clients is encrypted only if the sender chooses to, and deposit wire instructions go out as plain PDF attachments. Planned: send instructions only through the transaction platform's secure client document sharing, with a callback script.
Laptops have full-disk encryption (MSP report). Gaps: the 2 desktops are not encrypted, and the scanning workstation keeps local scans; contractor devices are unknown.
The MSP applies operating system and browser updates monthly and critical updates within 14 days, and reports monthly.
Signature antivirus on all 9 company devices, managed by the MSP. Gap: alerts reach the MSP in business hours only; no behavior-based detection.

Gap: no alerts on new forwarding rules, risky sign-ins, or bulk downloads; external auto-forwarding is allowed. Planned: built-in SYS-02 alerts sent to the Office Manager and the MSP, and external forwarding blocked, by 2026-10-31.

The vendor's spam and phishing filtering and an external-sender banner are on. Gaps: the domain's DMARC policy is monitor only and nobody reads the reports; no check for look-alike domains of the company or its title company partners.

Gap: no retention schedule; client files, ID images, and screening reports are kept indefinitely. Planned: a retention rule in POL-04 4.8: brokerage records 5 years as Fla. Stat. 475.5015 requires, screening reports 2 years after the decision, then secure disposal.
